problems.statement: FPGA card startup then logs `INIT: Environment setup failed. Aborting.` and exits with code 1.
problems.code_says: Only `get_devices()` logs that line and calls `std::exit(1)`, when its own `pos_startup()` call returns -1 (src/pos/driver.cpp:886-889). The check sits in `pos_heap_setup()`, which `pos_startup_host()` calls (src/pos/driver.cpp:290). 19 test source files call `pos_startup()` or `pos_startup_host()` themselves and handle the -1 return in their own way. Examples: t/t_dma.cpp:74 and t/t_blind_reset.cpp:25 throw `Error initializing libpos context`. t/t_init.cpp:11 logs `Environment setup failed. Aborting.` without the `INIT:` prefix and returns -1. t/t_heap.cpp:11 logs `Heap setup failed. Aborting.` and returns -1. t/t_alloc.cpp:22 returns -1 with no extra line. Some of these programs need hugepages only and no FPGA card (t/README.testing.md:28-35). So the second log line and exit code 1 hold only for a program whose first libpos call is `get_devices()`.
problems.corrected_cell: When a program runs as root and the variable exists, the hugepage heap setup fails with the log line `Please do not run as sudo`. A program that starts the FPGA cards through `get_devices()` then logs `INIT: Environment setup failed. Aborting.` and exits with code 1. A test program that calls `pos_startup()` or `pos_startup_host()` itself stops with its own message and exit code. `rinzler` and `runtron` never reach this check as root. They abort earlier with `fuse_sysfs must not run as root`, with or without the variable. The check stops a hardware test program that runs under `sudo`. A root process without the variable passes the check.

notes: Result: 9 rows correct, 1 row imprecise (SUDO_USER), 0 rows wrong. All 10 variables were searched with git grep in the checkout at commit 7eddde7895, and the code around every read and every set was read. Nothing was built or run. Observations that were not graded as problems, because they do not change what a reader would do: (1) DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_SPAWN_OK: bin/dice-tests/test_daemon_lifecycle.py:231 also sets the variable to 1 in one test, and the Set by cell names only bin/dice. (2) DICE_GRANT_ID: on a host without shared Dice, bin/rinzler:309 and bin/runtron:328 remove the variable from the environment of the native program, and bin/slice:2232 also writes the id into the benchmark lock holder record. The row does not mention either. The wrappers and bin/slice exit with status 2 only when DICE_DAEMON_CHILD is exactly 1, and the row says 'set'. (3) FAKE_TRACED_EXIT_AFTER_CAPTURE_READY: the fake traced also waits for the file named by FAKE_TRACED_CAPTURE_MARKER before it exits (perfetto/test_perfetto.py:185). The neighbouring row for that variable says so. (4) REMOTE_MODEL: the remote mode can also come from TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION when REMOTE is undefined (GNUmakefile:130-133). The REMOTE row covers this. (5) FUSE_STATS_STAMP: 'make -e' (environment overrides makefile assignments) was not considered by the row and is not graded. (6) SUDO_USER: the Read by cell says 'hardware test programs', but hugepage-only test programs such as t_heap and t_alloc reach the same check without any FPGA card.
